'''Richard Alfred Matzner''' is an American [[physicist]], working mostly in the field of [[general relativity]] and [[cosmology]], including [[numerical relativity]], kinetic theory, [[black hole]] physics, and [[gravitational radiation]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/998239 |title= Richard Matzner in INSPIRE High Energy Physics Database |publisher= CERN, DESY, Fermilab, IHEP, IN2P3, and SLAC |access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref> He is Professor of Physics at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] where he directed the Center for Relativity.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ph.utexas.edu/component/cobalt/item/18-physics/449-matzner-richard-a?Itemid=1264 |title=Richard Matzner at the University of Texas at Austin Department of Physics|language=en|access-date=2023-08-14}}</ref> In 1993 he organized and was Lead Principal Investigator of an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]]/[[Advanced Research Projects Agency|ARPA]] funded computational [[Grand Challenge]] program involving ten university teams seeking computational descriptions for the interaction of black holes as potential sources for observable gravitational radiation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Thorne |first1=Kip |date=2018-12-18 |title=Nobel Lecture: LIGO and gravitational waves III |journal=Rev. Mod. Phys. |volume=90 |issue=40503 |article-number=040503 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.90.040503 |bibcode=2018RvMP...90d0503T |s2cid=125431568 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Matzner |first1=Richard |last2=Seidel |first2=H |date=1995-11-10 |title=Geometry of a Black Hole Collision |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.270.5238.941 |journal=Science |volume=270 |issue=5238 |pages=941–947 |doi=10.1126/science.270.5238.941 |bibcode=1995Sci...270..941M |s2cid=121172545 |access-date=2023-09-24|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His work leading what became known as the [[Binary Black Hole Grand Challenge Alliance]]<ref>{{cite conference |last1=Choptuik |first1=M. |date=1997 |title= The Binary Black Hole Grand Challenge Project |conference=12th Kingston Meeting on Theoretical Astrophysics; proceedings of meeting held in Halifax; Nova Scotia; Canada October 17–19, 1996 |url=https://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1997ASPC..123..305C |journal=Computational Astrophysics |volume=123 |issue=ASP Conference Series |editor= D. A. Clarke and M. J. West |pages=305–313 |bibcode=1997ASPC..123..305C |access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.crpc.rice.edu/CRPC/demos/BlackHole/ |title=Binary Black Hole Grand Challenge Alliance page at Center for Research on Parallel Computing at Rice University|language=en|access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Jani |first1=Karan |title=Exclusive: Interview With Kip Thorne, One of the Winners of 2017 Physics Nobel |url=https://thewire.in/science/its-your-generation-of-experimenters-that-makes-me-look-good-an-interview-with-kip-thorne |access-date=6 November 2023 |work=The Wire |publisher=The Wire |date=3 October 2017}}</ref> featured in [[Kip Thorne]]'s [[Nobel Prize]] lecture, including when Matzner and Alliance collaborators wagered Thorne that [[numerical relativity]] would produce a simulated waveform comparable to observation prior to the first [[LIGO]] detection.  Matzner and colleagues eventually won, Thorne saying he "conceded the bet with great happiness."<ref>{{cite speech |last=Thorne |first=Kip S. |author-link= NobelPrize.org |title= Kip S. Thorne – Nobel Lecture|event= Nobel Prize Ceremony |date=2017-12-08 |location=Stockholm University |publisher= Nobel Prize Outreach AB 2023 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2017/thorne/lecture/ |access-date=2023-09-19 |language=English}}</ref>
 
==Education and career==
Matzner received his Ph.D. from the University of Maryland in Physics in 1967, advised by [[Charles Misner]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cmns.umd.edu/news-events/news/gravitational-waves |title=A Brief History of Gravitational Waves Research at the University of Maryland|date=10 November 2021 |language=en|access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref> He concluded his graduate education with a year at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="Jeff fellows">{{cite web |url=https://sites.nationalacademies.org/cs/groups/pgasite/documents/webpage/pga_059676.pdf |title=National Academies: Jefferson Science Fellows 2004 – 2017 |language=en |access-date=2023-08-14}}</ref> Matzner has advised and educated students in cosmology, relativity, and astrophysics.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ali |first=Eunice |date=2016-02-14 |title= UT alumnus leads team in detecting gravitational waves, confirms Einstein's theory |url=https://thedailytexan.com/2016/02/13/ut-alumnus-leads-team-in-detecting-gravitational-waves-confirms-einsteins-theory/ |work=The Daily Texan |location=Austin, Texas |access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=45779&fChrono=1 |title=Mathematics Genealogy Project on Richard Matzner|language=en|access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref> He was one of the first to calculate what a simplified, head-on collision between two black holes would look like, including the weak gravitational waves such a merger could emit.<ref>{{cite news |last= Wright |first= Matthew |date= 2016-10-29 |title=The Chirps Heard Round the World |url=https://cmns.umd.edu/news-events/news/chirps-heard-round-world |work=Odyssey magazine |location=University of Maryland |access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the American Physical Society in 1995 for "his analyses in general relativity of a wide range of astrophysical phenomena, especially his numerical simulations of strong-field gravitational systems and the gravitational radiation they produce."<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=M |website=www.aps.org |publisher=American Physical Society |access-date=7 November 2023 |language=en}}</ref> Matzner's research in theoretical questions includes topology and signature change in the early universe, and quantum gravity using the tool of path integration.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=richard+matzner |title=Richard Matzner in zbMATH |language=en|access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1= Ellis |first1=G. F. R. |last2=Rothman |first2=Tony |chapter= THE GARDEN OF COSMOLOGICAL DELIGHTS |title=Science a La Mode: Physical Fashions and Fictions |publisher=Princeton University Press, JSTOR |year=1989 |pages= 3–28 |jstor=j.ctt7zvs2k.4. }}</ref> His observational/experimental studies include tests of [[General Relativity|General Relativistic]] effects via [[LAGEOS|laser-ranging]] to dense geodetic satellites.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Richard-Matzner |title=ResearchGate database results on Richard Matzner|language=en|access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ciufolini |first1=Ignazio |last2=Paolozzi |first2=Antonio |last3=Pavlis |first3=Erricos C. |last4=Ries |first4=John |last5=Koenig |first5=Rolf |last6=Matzner |first6=Richard |last7=Sindoni |first7=Giampiero |last8=Neumayer |first8=Hans |title=Testing gravitational physics with satellite laser ranging |journal=The European Physical Journal Plus |date=11 August 2011 |volume=126 |issue=8 |page=72 |doi=10.1140/epjp/i2011-11072-2 |bibcode=2011EPJP..126...72C |s2cid=122205903 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1140/epjp/i2011-11072-2 |access-date=7 November 2023 |language=en |issn=2190-5444|url-access=subscription }}</ref> These experiments resulted in the first (and best as of 2023) measurement and confirmation of the Lens-Thirring [[frame-dragging]] effect, predicted by Einstein's theory of general relativity, to within 10 percent.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Will |first1=Clifford M. |title=Finally, results from Gravity Probe B |journal=Physics |date=31 May 2011 |volume=4 |issue=22 |page=43 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.221101 |pmid=21702590 |url=https://physics.aps.org/articles/v4/43 |access-date=6 November 2023 |language=en|doi-access=free |arxiv=1105.3456 }}</ref> Matzner is Co-I of the [[LARES (satellite)|LARES]] (Laser Relativity Satellite) satellite team, the densest artificial satellite in orbit, launched in 2012,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ilrs.gsfc.nasa.gov/missions/satellite_missions/current_missions/lars_general.html |title=NASA LARES Mission page LARES|language=en|access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref> with a second satellite, [[LARES (satellite)|LARES 2]], launched in 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Home - Lares Mission |url=https://www.lares-mission.com/default.asp?language=en |website=www.lares-mission.com |publisher=LARES Mission Lab |access-date=6 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://oden.utexas.edu/people/directory/Richard-Matzner/ |title=Richard Matzner in Oden Institute Directory|language=en|access-date=2023-08-14}}</ref>

==Policy, Outreach, & Diplomacy==

Matzner served on advisory committees to the [[US Air Force]], the [[National Science Foundation]], the [[National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine#Program units|National Research Council]], the [[European Space Agency]], and the [[Department of Energy]], such as the committee which determined relativity was needed for time transfer accuracy in satellite systems ([[GPS]]).<ref name="UT exp">{{Cite web |url=https://experts.utexas.edu/richard_matzner |title=Richard Matzner in UT Experts|language=en |access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite report |author1=Andreas Albrecht |author2=Stefi Baum |author3=Sarah Church |author4=Debra Elmegreen |author5=Joshua Frieman |author6=Martha Haynes |author7=Gregory Laughlin |author8=Mordecai-Mark Mac Low |author9=Richard Matzner |url=https://www.nsf.gov/mps/ast/aaac/reports/annual/aaac_2012_report.pdf |publisher=National Science Foundation |access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite report |author1=Andreas Albrecht |author2=Stefi Baum |author3=James Buckley |author4=William Cochran |author5=Priscilla Cushman |author6=Debra Elmegreen |author7=Joshua Frieman |author8=Martha Haynes |author9=Mordecai-Mark Mac Low |url=https://www.nsf.gov/mps/ast/aaac/reports/annual/aaac_2013_130308finalreport.pdf |publisher=National Science Foundation |access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite report |author1=Andreas Albrecht |author2=Stefi Baum |author3=James Buckley |author4=William Cochran |author5=Priscilla Cushman |author6=Craig Hogan |author7=Mordecai-Mark Mac Low |author8=Geoffrey Marcy |author9=Richard Matzner |author10=Angela Olinto |author11=Paula Szkody |author12=Angela Speck |author13=Suzanne Staggs |date= 2014-03-15 |title= Report of the Astronomy and Astrophysics Advisory Committee |url=https://www.nsf.gov/mps/ast/aaac/reports/annual/aaac_2014_report.pdf |publisher=National Science Foundation |access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nsf.gov/mps/ast/aaac/members/2011-12_bios/richard_matzner.pdf |title=National Science Foundation Astronomy and Astrophysics Advisory Committee Members Bio on Richard Matzner |language=en|access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Accuracy of Time Transfer in Satellite Systems |journal=The National Academies Press |date=1 January 1986 |doi=10.17226/19205 |url=https://nap.nationalacademies.org/catalog/19205/accuracy-of-time-transfer-in-satellite-systems |access-date=16 November 2023 |publisher=National Academies Press |bibcode=1986nap..book19205N |isbn=978-0-309-32099-3 |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He was on research assignment at Los Alamos National Laboratory,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/6389512 |title=Los Alamos National Laboratory archives, DOE Office of Scientific and Technical Information |date=January 1991 |language=en|access-date=2023-09-24 |last1=Laguna |first1=P. |last2=Kurki-Suonio |first2=H. |last3=Matzner |first3=R. A.}}</ref> in the Institute for Geophysics and Planetary Physics, beginning a Dictionary of Geophysics, Astrophysics, and Astronomy.<ref name="UT exp" /> His science outreach activities<ref>{{cite news |last=Bloodworth |first=Sarah |date=2017-05-03 |title= Sci-Fact Column: Rick, Morty and the multiverse |url=https://thedailytexan.com/2017/05/03/sci-fact-column-rick-morty-and-the-multiverse/ |work=The Daily Texan |location=Austin, TX |access-date=2023-09-24}}</ref> include appointment to the [[United States Department of State#Jefferson Science Fellows Program|Jefferson Science Fellows]] at the [[US Department of State]], which placed Matzner as Senior Science Advisor in the East Asia and Pacific Bureau at the U.S. State Department.<ref name="Jeff fellows" /><ref name="Nat Acad">{{Cite web |url=https://sites.nationalacademies.org/pga/Jefferson/PGA_070563 |title=Richard Matzner in National Academies Directory|language=en|access-date=2023-08-14}}</ref> He advised on subjects including "Space and Cyber questions, Health, Environmental and Climate Change and its effect on the oceans, topics relating to Energy and to Scarce Material resources, on Innovation, and on Commercialization of academic research" and "contributed to and participated in meetings on space security in Vietnam and Malaysia, and on joint scientific commission meetings with Malaysia and Australia."<ref name="Nat Acad" /> Matzner participated on scientific editorial boards,<ref name="Jeff fellows" /><ref name="Nat Acad" /> served for a decade as Southwest Region Lead Judge for the Siemens/Westinghouse Science Competition, and co-directed international summer schools on Relativistic Astrophysics in Erice, Italy.<ref name="Jeff fellows" /><ref name="Nat Acad" /> His international collaborations and long-term visits include at institutes in Britain ([[University of Oxford]]), France, Germany (external advisory committee to the [[Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics]]), Turkey, and Italy (Aerospace Engineering Department at [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]] on laser ranged satellites<ref name="Jeff fellows" /><ref name="Nat Acad" /> and [[theory of relativity|relativistic]] [[astrophysics]] lecture series at the [[University of Salento|University]] in [[Lecce]]).<ref name="Nat Acad" /><ref>{{cite sign |title = International School on Astrophysical Relativity  |year = 2006
|type        = poster
|publisher   = NASA, Ettore Majorana Foundation, World Federation of Scientists
|location = Sicily, Italy
|url = https://ilrs.gsfc.nasa.gov/docs/2006/Erice2006_FINAL.pdf |access-date = 2023-09-24}}</ref>
